free_tier.stated: 100 MB per file, 10 GB per project — both are *defaults*, both are raisable by filing a GitHub issue. Unlimited number of projects. Verified in warehouse source: MAX_FILESIZE = 100 * ONE_MIB, MAX_PROJECT_SIZE = 10 * ONE_GIB, UPLOAD_LIMIT_CAP = 1 GiB.

retention.stated: | Deletion is permanent and irreversible ('cannot be undone without administrative intervention')

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. files.pythonhosted.org probe: Server: cloudflare, Cache-Control: 'max-age=365000000, immutable, public', Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, no auth.

tooling: Legacy upload API POST /legacy/ (twine), JSON API GET /pypi/<name>/json for metadata, direct file GET from files.pythonhosted.org. Orgs/teams exist. Named wrapper class: pypi/* tools, twine, and warehouse itself. No rclone backend.
chaining: UNBOUNDED via projects: unlimited projects x 10 GB each (raisable to 40 GB — uv and ruff were both granted 40 GB). 10 TiB = 1,024 projects at default 10 GB. Project creation is rate limited to 20/hour and 40/hour per IP, which is the binding constraint, not bytes.
limits_note: 100 MB/file, 10 GB/project (both raisable; 40 GB grants are routine for large projects). 20 project creations/hour/user, 10/day/organization, 40/hour/IP (warehouse config.py defaults). Files cannot be uploaded to a release older than 14 days (MAXIMUM_AGE_FOR_NEW_UPLOADS). Deleting a file frees quota; yanking does NOT.
reliability_note: Deletion is permanent and irreversible ('cannot be undone without administrative intervention'). Releases are append-only in practice but files *can* be deleted to free project quota, so unlike npm this is not immutable-by-design — treat it as stable-but-deletable. Quota enforcement is a hard 400 at upload, so budget against the 10 GB project figure.
